maya: heads up — we missed ~2h of metering events this morning for eu-west due to a routing policy flip. billing ingestion shows a hole between 08:14–10:12 UTC. noticed via anomaly alert on the cost dashboard :eyes:

oliver: Ugh. Which layer dropped events — proxy, router, or the ingest forwarder?

maya: seems like the routing policy change (route-by-tenant -> route-by-region) briefly returned `route_key` null for some legacy customers. proxy forwarded, but the metering lambda filtered null route_keys out. logs attached: `ERROR: metering.ingest - missing_route_key, customer_id=acct_42`

dina: can we do a cheap backfill that derives route_key from request metadata? The requests still exist in request-log topic. We should rehydrate metering events rather than retro-billing if counts are the same.

raj: +1 on reconstructing from request-log. Only concern is cost-allocation mapping: some requests were later routed to a cheaper model variant; do we attribute to original routing decision or final served variant?

oliver: Good point. Current invoice mapping uses `served_variant` when available for cost-per-token. But our metering pipeline expects `route_key` for quota attribution. If we backfill from request-log we can fetch both and attach both fields: `route_key` (for quota) and `served_variant` (for pricing). Then billing job can pick pricing field.

maya: plan: 1) run selector to find affected request ids 2) replay request-log -> metering topic with patched route_key 3) run aggregation job to compute delta metrics 4) mark invoices for manual review if delta>threshold. Anyone object?

dina: sounds fine. Can you paste the query to select affected requests?

maya: sure — quick KSQL: ```
SELECT req_id, customer_id, served_variant, metadata -> 'region' as region
FROM request_log
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-17T08:14:00Z' AND '2026-03-17T10:12:00Z'
  AND (metadata -> 'route_key' IS NULL OR metadata -> 'route_key' = '')
EMIT CHANGES;
```

raj: For safety, can we run a dry-run to compute token deltas? Something like: ```sql
WITH reconstructed AS (
  SELECT req_id, tokens, COALESCE(metadata->'route_key', derive_route_key(metadata)) AS route_key
  FROM request_log WHERE ts BETWEEN X AND Y
)
SELECT route_key, SUM(tokens) AS tokens_missing FROM reconstructed GROUP BY route_key;
```
This will show how quotas are affected.

maya: I ran the dry-run locally — totals per tenant look small (mostly <0.5% of monthly volume) but a couple of enterprise tenants show spikes ~5k tokens.

billing-bot: alert: invoice-impact-check failed for acct_99 — delta 0.42% of billed tokens.

oliver: For any tenant with >0.1% delta we should create a billing ticket and notify CS. Also add a flag in the invoice history: `metering_source=backfill_2026-03-17`.

dina: Agreed. Also we need to update the console dashboards so the spike is annotated as a backfill and not a regression in model usage. Otherwise product teams will freak out.

maya: deployment note: I'm going to run the backfill job via the batch-worker cluster. Command: `./tools/backfill --from 2026-03-17T08:14 --to 2026-03-17T10:12 --source request-log --attach route_key,served_variant --dry-run=false`

raj: Please add `--max-rate 2000` to avoid downstream write pressure on metering topic. Also ensure dedupe by req_id: we must not double-count if some events already arrived later.

maya: yep adding dedupe. Will run at 11:30 UTC once I patch the router to keep route_key populated.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: running job backfill/2026-03-17-11:30, ETA ~35m. Logs: https://logs.redwood.example/backfill/2026-03-17-11:30

oliver: After backfill, can we run the aggregation and then a diff job against invoices to auto-generate adjustment proposals? Something lightweight — don't auto-charge/credit.

dina: +1 — CS should approve adjustments before applying. We should also surface adjustment candidates in the internal billing console with accept/reject buttons.

maya: agreed. I'll produce a CSV with columns: `acct, original_tokens, new_tokens, token_delta, suggested_credit_usd, notes` and upload to shared drive.

raj: quick note: let's update the routing policy rollout checklist to include a metering smoke test (send 50 synthetic requests across tenants and verify `route_key` persists). Prevents recurrence.

maya: action items: 1) maya run backfill (11:30) 2) maya upload CSV + jira billing-ticket for any tenant >0.1% delta 3) devex add metering smoke test to rollout checklist 4) billing/product notification templates — dina

dina: I'll draft the email + CS playbook.

oliver: thanks team. ping me when the CSV is ready and we'll coordinate with finance for invoice annotations. :+1:
